overview: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple (Dharmapuri Kshetram) in Dharmapuri, Jagtial District, Telangana, is one of the oldest and most revered Narasimha temples in South India. The presiding deity is Lord Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy, the man-lion incarnation (4th avatar) of Lord Vishnu, seen seated in Padmasana (Yoga Mudra) with Goddess Lakshmi — a posture considered rare. The temple sits on the southern bank of the Godavari River, which uniquely flows southward (Dakshina Vahini) here — a rare and highly auspicious geographical feature, earning Dharmapuri the epithet 'Dakshina Kashi' (Southern Varanasi) and 'Banaras of South India'. The town is also a 'Hari-Hara Kshetra' — a rare confluence of Vaishnava and Shaiva traditions, with both the Lakshmi Narasimha temple and several ancient Shiva temples in the sacred town. The complex includes the Pata (Old) Narasimha temple and the Kottha (New) Narasimha temple, reflecting cycles of destruction and reconstruction. It is one of the nine Nava Narasimha Kshetrams, has one of the largest settlements of Vedic Brahmins in Telangana, and is also called 'Teertharajamu' (king of pilgrimages). The next Godavari Pushkaralu will be hosted here in 2027.
summary: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple (Dharmapuri Kshetram) in Dharmapuri, Jagtial District, Telangana, is an ancient Narasimha shrine (built c. 850–928 AD / 1018 AD per inscriptions; rebuilt multiple times) on the southern bank of the Dakshina Vahini Godavari River, where the Godavari uniquely flows southward. One of the nine Nava Narasimha Kshetrams and a 'Hari-Hara Kshetra', it houses the rare Padmasana-form of Lakshmi Narasimha with Goddess Lakshmi, plus shrines to Ugra/Yoga/Saumya Narasimha forms, Lord Venkateswara, Lord Brahma (rare 6-ft, four-faced murti), eight Hanumans, and Lord Yama. The town has both a Pata (Old) and a Kottha (New) Narasimha temple from cycles of destruction and reconstruction (the Kottha built in 1803 AD by Panatula Narayana Deekshitulu). It is busiest during the 13-day Brahmotsavam (Phalguna Shuddha Ekadashi to Ashtami, Feb/Mar), Narasimha Jayanthi, Vaikuntha Ekadashi and the Godavari Pushkaralu (next: 2027).

history.content: The temple has a history spanning more than a millennium. The construction period is variously cited as 850–928 AD (Trawell) and 1018 AD (per Tripadvisor reviewer citing inscriptions); the temple was originally built by the Chalukya dynasty, with later patronage from the Rashtrakutas and the Kakatiyas. Dharmapuri has long been one of the largest settlements of Vedic Brahmins in Telangana and a centre of Vedic learning, literature, and fine arts. The town is named after King Dharma Varma, who laid the foundation of the Lord's shrine. The temple is referenced in ancient texts like the Skanda Purana and Brahmanda Purana as 'Dharmapura', and is linked to legends of Lord Narasimha's meditation after slaying the demon Hiranyakashipu to protect his devotee Prahlada. It is also believed that Lord Rama visited this site and installed a sacred linga here.

history.content: The temple was demolished by Muslim rulers during 1422–1436 AD (Rustumdil Khan, the Subedar of Hyderabad, with the support of Aurangzeb, is said to have converted it to a mosque), and was rebuilt in the 17th century, regaining its status as a major Vaishnava shrine. The Kottha (New) Narasimha Swamy Temple, also known as Sri Ugra Narasimha Swamy Temple, was built in 1803 AD by Panatula Narayana Deekshitulu and stands to the right of the Pata Narasimha temple. The temple is administered by the Telangana Endowments Department (one of 19 major temples with annual income above ₹1 crore, per the 2015 Trust Board notification). For the 2027 Godavari Pushkaralu, the Telangana government has allocated ₹50 crore for renovation, including ₹80 lakh for a new toilet complex and ₹3.1 crore for four VIP suites. The temple is a major centre for Vedic Brahmin scholars in Telangana and one of the nine Nava Narasimha Kshetrams.

sthala_puranam: Dharmapuri is named after King Dharma Varma, who laid the foundation of the Lord's shrine. The temple's most distinctive feature is its location on the banks of the Dakshina Vahini Godavari — a stretch where the Godavari, unusually, flows southward, a direction considered highly auspicious in Hindu tradition. The town is also called 'Dakshina Kashi' (Southern Varanasi) and 'Banaras of South India', and is a 'Hari-Hara Kshetra' — a rare confluence of Vaishnava and Shaiva traditions. The temple is referenced in the Skanda Purana and Brahmanda Purana as 'Dharmapura', and is linked to legends of Lord Narasimha's meditation after slaying Hiranyakashipu. The town's dual Pata (Old) and Kottha (New) Narasimha temples reflect its passage through medieval destruction (1422–1436 AD) and reconstruction. Pilgrims traditionally take a holy dip in the Godavari before entering the temple, believing it purifies body and soul.
religious_significance: Dharmapuri is regarded as one of the holiest Narasimha temples in South India and one of the Nava Narasimha Kshetrams (nine major Narasimha shrines). It is a rare 'Hari-Hara Kshetra' — a confluence of Vaishnava and Shaiva traditions, with both the Lakshmi Narasimha temple and several ancient Shiva temples in the sacred town. It is also called 'Dakshina Kashi' (Southern Varanasi) and 'Teertharajamu' (king of pilgrimages). Lord Narasimha is worshipped here as the protector of righteousness and the destroyer of evil. The presiding deity in Padmasana (Yoga Mudra) is considered a rare form.
spiritual_significance: Devotees believe sincere prayers remove fear, protect families, and bring peace, prosperity and spiritual growth. The temple houses multiple forms of Lord Narasimha — peaceful and fierce manifestations (Yoga, Ugra, Saumya). The Dakshina Vahini Godavari holy bath is central to its spiritual practice, believed to purify body and soul. The temple is especially sought for protection, courage, prosperity, relief from difficulties, and for child-related and family blessings. Devotees also perform Gho Pooja for wealth and for removal of enemies.

architecture: The temple reflects a Dravidian style with towering gopurams, intricate carvings depicting scenes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata, and spacious mandapams including the Mukha, Garuda and Kalyana halls, leading to the sanctum via the Simha Dwaram (Lion Gate). The main deity is in a serene Padmasana (Yoga Mudra) pose flanked by Goddess Lakshmi. The complex includes three forms of Narasimha — Yoga, Ugra and Saumya — and rare sub-shrines: an idol of Yama (Dharmaraju) at the entrance, eight Hanuman murtis, and a unique 6-foot, four-faced Brahma murti (one of the few in South India). Smaller shrines house Lord Venkateswara, Sri Venugopala Swamy, Sri Prasannanjaneya Swamy, Sri Ramalingeshwara Swamy, and a Pushkarini (temple tank). The Pata (Old) and Kottha (New) Narasimha temples stand side by side. Per dharmapurikshetram.in, the temple is being prepared for the 2027 Pushkaralu with new toilet complexes and VIP suites.

festivals.festival: Brahmotsavam (Dharmapuri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Aalaya Jatara)
festivals.description: The most significant annual festival — a 13-day celebration held from Phalguna Shuddha Ekadashi to Phalguna Shuddha Ashtami (Feb/Mar). 2025: 10–22 March (per Deccan Chronicle). 2026: 27 February – 11 March (per sanatanavibes). Highlights include Ankurarpana, the divine wedding (Kalyanotsavam) of Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy and Sri Venkateswara Swamy, Teppotsavam (float festival on the Godavari), Dolotsavam of Sri Yoga Narasimha Swamy, the Muvvur Swamulu chariot procession, and grand processions. Guided spiritually by Paramahamsa Parivrājaka Āchārya (head of Dharmapuri Mutt) and Sri Sri Sri Satchidananda Saraswati Maharaj.

darshan_and_tickets.general_darshan: General darshan is free for all devotees.
darshan_and_tickets.special_darshan: Special seva tickets are available at the temple counter per the published tariff.
darshan_and_tickets.ticket_details: Paid sevas include Abhishekam (₹150), Nitya Kalyanam (₹500), Sudarshana Homam (₹316), Kumkumarchana (₹100), various bhogam offerings (Pulihora Bhogam ₹100, Bhoorela Bhogam ₹150, Ammavari Odebiyyam ₹25), Vahana Seva (₹1,516), Nitya Rathaseva (₹300), Marriage (₹2,116), Upanayanam (₹1,516), Keshakandanam (₹20), Swamy Aarti (₹10), Ganda Deepam (₹5), Vehicle Pooja (₹100 / ₹50), and Saswatha (perpetual) endowment poojas (₹1,116 to ₹25,116). During Brahmotsavam, Narasimha Jayanthi and Vaikuntha Ekadashi, separate crowd-management arrangements are provided. The Telangana government has allocated ₹3.1 crore for four new VIP suites as part of Pushkaralu 2027 preparations.

dress_code: Devotees are expected to wear traditional and modest attire. Men generally wear dhoti, kurta or formal Indian clothing; women are encouraged to wear sarees, salwar kameez or other traditional dresses. Shorts, sleeveless clothing and revealing outfits are discouraged. Footwear must be removed before entering, silence should be maintained in the sanctum, and photography may be restricted near the main deity.

accommodation.availability: The temple offers guest houses and dharmashalas with basic amenities at affordable prices, plus several private hotels, lodges and guest houses in Dharmapuri town (budget and deluxe). The sacred town also has choultries. Nearby towns Jagtial (~30 km), Mancherial (~40 km), Karimnagar (~70–75 km) and Ramagundam (~65 km) offer more options, including premium accommodation.
accommodation.booking_process: Advance booking is recommended for Brahmotsavam, Narasimha Jayanthi, Vaikuntha Ekadashi and Godavari Pushkaralu due to heavy demand. Live temple and Pushkaralu 2027 updates are available via the dharmapurikshetram.in WhatsApp channel.
accommodation.price_range: Temple guest rooms ~₹300–₹800 per day (family/special rooms higher). Private hotels and lodges in Dharmapuri ~₹800–₹2,500 per night.
nearby_options: Budget, family and premium hotels in Dharmapuri town

best_time_to_visit: October to March (October–February excellent) for pleasant weather and comfortable Godavari holy baths. Best days: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday; best time 5:30–8:00 AM, evening option 4:00–6:00 PM. Most spiritually enriching during the 13-day Brahmotsavam (Phalguna Shuddha Ekadashi to Ashtami, Feb/Mar), Narasimha Jayanthi (Vaisakha), Vaikuntha Ekadashi (December) and Godavari Pushkaralu (next: 26 June – 7 July 2027, very crowded).

travel.road: Approximately 220–245 km from Hyderabad (4–5 hours). TGSRTC operates regular buses from Hyderabad, Karimnagar, Jagtial, Warangal, Nizamabad, Mancherial, Ramagundam and Peddapalli; APSRTC connects from Andhra Pradesh. Special buses run during Brahmotsavam, Narasimha Jayanthi and Godavari Pushkaralu.
travel.rail: Nearest station is Mancherial Railway Station (~40 km), connected to Hyderabad, Secunderabad, Vijayawada, Nagpur, Delhi, Chennai and Visakhapatnam. Taxis, auto-rickshaws and TGSRTC buses are available from the station.

Located on the sacred banks of the Godavari River, the event will be marked by grandeur and devotion. The festivities will be guided spiritually by Paramahamsa Parivrājaka Āchārya, head of Dharmapuri Mutt, and Sri Sri Sri Satchidananda Saraswati Maharaj. Highlights include the divine wedding of Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy and Sri Venkateswara Swamy on March 11, followed by a ritual float procession (Teppotsavam) and Dolotsavam of Sri Yoga Narasimha Swamy on March 14.'

introduction.en: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, popularly known as Dharmapuri Temple, in Dharmapuri, Jagtial District, Telangana, is one of the oldest and most revered Narasimha temples in South India, standing on the southern bank of the Godavari River where it uniquely flows southward — the Dakshina Vahini. One of the nine Nava Narasimha Kshetrams and a 'Hari-Hara Kshetra', it is also called 'Dakshina Kashi' and 'Banaras of South India'. The presiding deity is Lord Lakshmi Narasimha in the rare Padmasana (Yoga Mudra) form, with Goddess Lakshmi. The complex includes the Pata (Old) and Kottha (New) Narasimha temples, plus rare sub-shrines including a six-foot four-faced Brahma murti. It draws thousands of pilgrims, especially during the 13-day Brahmotsavam, Narasimha Jayanthi, Vaikuntha Ekadashi and the Godavari Pushkaralu (next: 2027).

history.en: The temple is over a thousand years old, built c. 850 to 928 AD or 1018 AD per inscriptions, originally by the Chalukya dynasty and later patronised by the Rashtrakutas and Kakatiyas. Per legend, King Dharma Varma laid the foundation of the Lord's shrine, giving the town its name. The temple was demolished by Rustumdil Khan, the Subedar of Hyderabad, with Aurangzeb's support in 1422 to 1436 AD, and was rebuilt in the 17th century. The Kottha Narasimha Temple was built in 1803 AD by Panatula Narayana Deekshitulu. The temple is referenced in the Skanda Purana and Brahmanda Purana as 'Dharmapura', and is one of the 19 major temples with non-hereditary Trust Boards under the Telangana Endowments Department.

travel_guide.en: Dharmapuri Temple is about 220 to 245 kilometres from Hyderabad, a four to five hour drive, with TGSRTC and APSRTC buses. The nearest railway station is Mancherial, about 40 kilometres away, connected to Hyderabad, Nagpur, Delhi and Chennai. The nearest airports are Hyderabad, 220 to 250 kilometres, and Nagpur, about 330 kilometres. The temple is open from 5:00 AM with Suprabhata Seva, and the official darshan hours are 5:30 AM to 2:30 PM and 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM daily; some sources give 5:00 AM to 2:00 PM and 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM. The next Godavari Pushkaralu is 26 June to 7 July 2027. October to March is the best season.

faq.question: Where is Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple located?
faq.answer: The temple is located in Dharmapuri, Dharmapuri Mandal, Jagtial District, Telangana, on the southern bank of the Godavari River (Dakshina Vahini). Pincode 505425. About 220–245 km from Hyderabad; ~30 km from Jagtial; ~40 km from Mancherial Railway Station.

faq.question: Which deity is worshipped in the temple?
faq.answer: The presiding deity is Lord Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy (the 4th incarnation of Lord Vishnu) in the rare Padmasana (Yoga Mudra) form, accompanied by Goddess Lakshmi. The complex also includes three forms of Narasimha (Yoga, Ugra, Saumya), Lord Venkateswara, eight Hanuman murtis, a rare 6-ft four-faced Brahma murti, Lord Yama at the entrance, and Lord Shiva shrines (Hari-Hara Kshetra).

faq.question: Why is Dharmapuri Temple famous?
faq.answer: It is famous for being one of the nine Nava Narasimha Kshetrams, for its location on the sacred Dakshina Vahini (southward-flowing) Godavari River, for being called 'Dakshina Kashi' (Southern Varanasi) and 'Teertharajamu' (king of pilgrimages), for the rare Padmasana-form of Lord Lakshmi Narasimha, and for its status as a Hari-Hara Kshetra (Vaishnava-Shaiva harmony). The town has one of the largest settlements of Vedic Brahmins in Telangana. The next Godavari Pushkaralu is 26 June – 7 July 2027.

faq.question: What are the temple timings?
faq.answer: Per the JustDial official listing and dharmapurikshetram.in: 5:30 AM–2:30 PM and 4:00 PM–8:00 PM daily. The temple opens with Suprabhata Seva at 5:00 AM. Some other sources (Tripadvisor, Trawell, Grokipedia) give 5:00 AM–2:00 PM and 4:00 PM–8:00 PM. The 2:30 PM–4:00 PM break for darshanam is confirmed. Hours are extended during the 13-day Brahmotsavam, Narasimha Jayanthi, Vaikuntha Ekadashi and Godavari Pushkaralu.

faq.question: Is there an entry fee for darshan?
faq.answer: No. General darshan is free for all devotees. Special sevas require paid tickets: Abhishekam ₹150, Nitya Kalyanam ₹500, Sudarshana Homam ₹316, Kumkumarchana ₹100, Marriage ₹2,116, Upanayanam ₹1,516, Ganda Deepam ₹5, Swamy Aarti ₹10, plus Saswatha (perpetual) endowment poojas ranging from ₹1,116 to ₹25,116.

faq.question: Which is the biggest festival celebrated here?
faq.answer: The 13-day Brahmotsavam (Phalguna Shuddha Ekadashi to Phalguna Shuddha Ashtami, Feb/Mar) is the most significant — with Kalyanotsavam, Teppotsavam (float festival on the Godavari), Dolotsavam of Sri Yoga Narasimha Swamy, and the Muvvur Swamulu chariot procession. The 2025 Brahmotsavam was 10–22 March; the 2026 one is 27 February – 11 March. Narasimha Jayanthi, Vaikuntha Ekadashi and the Godavari Pushkaralu (next: 2027) are also major celebrations.

faq.question: Are accommodation facilities available?
faq.answer: Yes. Temple guest houses and dharmashalas on-site (~₹300–₹800/day), plus private hotels and lodges in Dharmapuri town (~₹800–₹2,500/night), Jagtial (~30 km), Mancherial (~40 km), Karimnagar (~70–75 km) and Ramagundam (~65 km). For Brahmotsavam and Godavari Pushkaralu 2027, advance booking is essential; live updates are available via the dharmapurikshetram.in WhatsApp channel.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Dharmapuri Temple?
faq.answer: October to March (October–February excellent) for pleasant weather and comfortable Godavari holy baths. Best days: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday. Most spiritually enriching: the 13-day Brahmotsavam (Feb/Mar), Narasimha Jayanthi (Vaisakha), Vaikuntha Ekadashi (December) and the Godavari Pushkaralu (next: 26 June – 7 July 2027, very crowded).

faq.question: What is the Dakshina Vahini Godavari and why is it important?
faq.answer: The Godavari River, which generally flows west to east, uniquely flows from north to south (Dakshina Vahini) at Dharmapuri — a rare and highly auspicious geographical feature. Pilgrims traditionally take a holy dip in this stretch of the Godavari before entering the temple, believing it purifies body and soul. The site is called 'Dakshina Kashi' (Southern Varanasi) because of this feature. The next Godavari Pushkaralu at this site is 26 June – 7 July 2027.

faq.question: What is special about the Padmasana-form of Lord Lakshmi Narasimha here?
faq.answer: Unlike the usual fierce, standing form of Lord Narasimha, the presiding deity at Dharmapuri is seen seated in Padmasana (Yoga Mudra) with his palms bending on his knees, accompanied by Goddess Lakshmi. Such a yogic posture is considered a rare form of the Lord and is one of the temple's defining features. The main deity is flanked by three forms of Narasimha — Yoga, Ugra and Saumya — symbolising peaceful, fierce and gentle aspects of the Lord.
